title: Stay warm, cool and sheltered
short: Cold without heating, carbon monoxide, winter storms, heat
intro: Readings for keeping warm when the heating fails, heating without the danger of carbon monoxide, getting through a cold wave at home and on the road, and helping people who suffer most from cold or heat.

choices.label: It's freezing and the heating is out
choices.hint: Winter, a power cut, staying warm overnight

read.label: When the heating fails
read.note: In German. Heaters approved for indoor use, warm clothes, blankets and sleeping bags; windows shut, but air the rooms briefly.

read.label: Dress warmly and drink water
read.note: In Spanish. From the Spanish civil protection guide to severe weather: in the cold, thick clothes and closed shoes that cover the body, plenty to drink, and mouth and nose covered.

read.label: Heating without power
read.note: In German. Even oil and gas heating stop in a power cut; camping or paraffin stoves, planned with ventilation and a flue.

choices.label: Heating or cooking with fire or gas indoors
choices.hint: Carbon monoxide from heaters, stoves, grills, generators or candles

read.label: Carbon monoxide: what is safe indoors
read.note: In German. Only devices approved for indoor use; an open fire indoors can make carbon monoxide; fit a CO alarm.

read.label: No generator indoors
read.note: WHO advice after floods: never run a petrol or diesel generator indoors, and have gas and electrical appliances checked before you use them again.

read.label: Braziers and stoves in closed rooms
read.note: In Spanish. From the Spanish civil protection guide to severe weather: in cold and snow, braziers and wood, coal or gas stoves in closed rooms without ventilation can poison you.

choices.label: Get the home through a cold wave
choices.hint: Frozen pipes, supplies, a safe way to keep warm

read.label: Get the home ready for cold and snow
read.note: In Spanish. From the Spanish civil protection guide to severe weather: a stove, food and medicines in reserve, a portable radio, the roof and heating checked, and a tap left slightly open in a hard frost.

read.label: Frozen pipes, and dangers after the storm
read.note: A trickle of running water, checking pipes, power cuts, floods from melting snow, icy paths.

choices.label: Out in the cold, or stuck in the car
choices.hint: Snow on the road, ice on a lake, shovelling snow

read.label: If you are trapped in the car, stay in it
read.note: Avoid driving, stay in a trapped vehicle, drive slowly on snow; how to judge ice on ponds and lakes.

read.label: A winter kit for the car
read.note: Tyres, jump leads, a first aid kit, a charger, warm clothes, a shovel, a full tank.

read.label: Clearing snow without overdoing it
read.note: In Spanish. From the Spanish civil protection guide to severe weather, in a snowfall: do not overexert yourself clearing snow, protect your face, head and hands, and stay in if there is a blizzard.

choices.label: Older people, babies or animals in the cold

read.label: Check on people at risk
read.note: Family, friends and neighbours more likely to suffer in the cold, such as older and chronically ill people.

read.label: Pets and livestock
read.note: Enough food and water, and not too exposed to the cold.

choices.label: It's dangerously hot
choices.hint: A heat wave, no cooling, older people or babies at home

read.label: Drink enough, and check on older people and babies
read.note: From the IFRC's first aid guidelines, on dehydration: in hot weather, check regularly on older adults and babies.

read.label: Someone is overheated: cool them down
read.note: Stop and move somewhere cool, cool with water, and when to call for help.

choices.label: Told to stay indoors: gas, smoke or radiation

limits.text: Indoors, use only heaters and stoves approved for indoor use.
Carbon monoxide poisoning can kill, and an open fire indoors can cause it too. A tested CO alarm warns you.
Do not use a petrol or diesel generator indoors.
Get medical help if signs of hypothermia or frostbite appear.
Avoid overexertion in the cold, such as clearing snow: it can cause a cardiac arrest.
Keep windows and doors shut against the cold, but air the rooms briefly and regularly.
If you are trapped in a car in a winter storm, stay inside it.
Grey ice is too thin: ice should be clear blue and over 12 cm thick before you step on it.

Know the risks where you live, and the nearest medical help
